title: Data Center Power Demand Is Set to Surge, Raising New Climate Challenges: BloombergNEF | BloombergNEF
gist: A BloombergNEF report for Bloomberg Philanthropies projects data center power demand nearly quadrupling to 2,354 TWh (7% of global demand) by 2035, with 181 GW of on-site gas proposed alongside data centers (90%+ in the US) as developers chase speed to power. Faster grid connections are the cleaner path in the US/Europe, while coal-heavy emerging markets (India, Indonesia, Malaysia; Brazil the renewable exception) need added clean generation.

insights.claim: BloombergNEF expects global data center electricity demand to almost quadruple to 2,354 TWh by 2035, equal to about 7% of global electricity demand, per a report commissioned by Bloomberg Philanthropies.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: A ~4x load increase in a decade underpins multi-year demand for generation, grid equipment and clean-power procurement.

insights.claim: BNEF forecasts India's data center electricity demand to rise from 11 TWh in 2025 to 91 TWh in 2035, with existing coal plants supplying much of the near-term additional electricity under its Economic Transition Scenario.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Indian data center growth is a near-term tailwind for coal utilisation, but also for bilateral/captive solar and wind developers.

insights.claim: BNEF forecasts Malaysia's data center electricity demand to rise from 7 TWh in 2025 to 45 TWh by 2035, increasing near-term use of existing coal and gas plants and likely driving new gas capacity and coal life extensions longer term.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Malaysia's data center boom implies fossil asset life extensions and new gas build, alongside third-party solar contracting.

insights.claim: Grid connection delays for large loads in the US and Europe, combined with the financial rewards of energizing quickly, are pushing some data center developers to build on-site gas-fired generation while awaiting a grid connection.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Behind-the-meter gas turbines/engines are a beneficiary of interconnection queues; grid speed is the binding constraint.

insights.claim: BNEF has tracked 181 GW of announced gas-fired generation proposed alongside data centers, more than 90% of it in the US, though the pipeline varies widely in maturity and is an indication of potential scale rather than a forecast.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Gauge of potential gas-equipment and fuel demand from data centers, to be heavily discounted for attrition.
insights.quote: should be viewed as an indication of potential scale rather than a forecast of what will ultimately be built

insights.claim: If all announced on-site gas plants for US data centers were built and operated at BNEF's assumptions, they would emit about 345 MtCO2e per year, 152 MtCO2e more than supplying that capacity from average US grid power, equal to 10% of 2025 US power-sector emissions.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Scale of incremental emissions makes on-site gas a likely regulatory and ESG target for hyperscaler/developer climate commitments.
insights.locator: If all announced on-site gas plants

insights.claim: On-site gas plants intended as a bridge until grid connection may keep generating once online because the economics encourage continued operation, creating a longer-term fossil-fuel lock-in risk beyond annual emissions.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: 'Bridge' gas assets may have longer lives than marketed, supporting gas demand but raising stranded/lock-in policy risk.
insights.quote: the economics could encourage them to continue generating energy, creating a longer-term fossil-fuel lock-in risk
insights.locator: If all announced on-site gas plants

insights.claim: BNEF's Mark Daly argues the economics of AI are making speed to power a top priority for data center developers, and the climate outcome hinges on how fast grids connect them and whether cleaner generation is added alongside demand.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Time-to-power, not just power price, drives siting and generation choices for AI data centers.
insights.quote: The extraordinary economics around AI are making speed to power one of the most important priorities
insights.locator: Mark Daly, Head of Data Centers

insights.claim: In developed markets like the US and Europe, grid-connecting new data centers is the more sustainable option than on-site gas, making faster grid connections key to limiting near-term emissions and fossil lock-in, alongside continued power-system decarbonization.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Policy momentum likely favours interconnection reform and grid buildout, benefiting grid equipment and transmission players.
insights.locator: In developed markets such as the US and Europe

insights.claim: BNEF reviewed grid-connection acceleration policies across 17 markets, including faster connections, financial commitments, flexible connections, special zones and clean-power procurement, but finds limited empirical evidence yet on which works best.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: The policy toolkit is unproven; watch which markets actually shorten queue times as a lead indicator for data center siting.
insights.quote: there is currently limited empirical evidence to demonstrate which will be most effective
insights.locator: The report reviews policies across 17 markets

insights.claim: Where power systems remain heavily coal-reliant, grid-connected data centers can have a worse climate impact than those powered by on-site gas, reversing the developed-market conclusion.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: In coal-heavy emerging markets, the priority shifts to adding clean generation rather than speeding grid hookups.
insights.quote: grid-connected data centers can be even worse than those powered by on-site gas

insights.claim: BNEF expects almost all incremental generation for Brazil's data center demand through 2035 to come from renewables, with new demand potentially absorbing currently curtailed renewable output, although transmission remains a constraint.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Brazil is positioned as a clean-power data center destination; curtailed renewables gain an offtaker, transmission is the bottleneck.

insights.claim: Coal and gas supplied 82% of Indonesian state utility PLN's on-grid power in 2025, and current rules bar data centers from contracting directly with independent renewable generators, limiting their ability to tie demand to new clean capacity.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Indonesia's regulatory framework is a barrier for hyperscalers with clean-power commitments; watch for rule changes on direct contracting.

insights.claim: In India and Malaysia, data centers can procure clean power via bilateral, captive or third-party renewable contracts and are already backing new solar and wind projects, though in Malaysia network charges can affect the economics.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Corporate PPA/captive renewable pipelines in India and Malaysia are a growth channel tied to data center buildout.
